disposition_reason: The final-paper Fig. 3 prediction task and author-code cohort are recoverable, but the exact numerical final-publication baseline has not been independently confirmed in this review. The primary author preprint reports a candidate value, which is recorded as version-specific evidence rather than silently promoted to the final-paper target. Existing prescribed reconstruction and a new two-person modify panel cannot establish a same-task win. The canonical scope also contains held-out-participant drive/suppress effects and linguistic-feature controls; Fig. 3 alone cannot establish whole-registration success until that complete scope rule is resolved.

source_paper.title: Driving and suppressing the human language network using large language models

evidence.supports: Predicted sentence responses compared with the average language-network response of three evaluation participants.
Original train cohort, 1,000 baseline sentences, ridge/GPT2-XL encoding and prospective corpus-selected stimulus evaluation.
Distinct event-related three-person and blocked four-person experiments; response normalization and source condition contrasts.

evidence.locator: Author preprint version 4, 30 October 2023; Results: Model captures most explainable variance in new participants
evidence.supports: Version-specific report of Pearson r=0.43 over 1,500 stimuli and r=0.30 over baseline stimuli; this review has not independently confirmed final-publication numerical identity.

evidence.locator: Repository organization; Downloading data; Analyzing data and generating plots
evidence.supports: Named event-related data release, train/evaluation participant distinction, model activations and fit/apply entrypoints.

evidence.locator: Settings and Figure 3 input-selection source cells
evidence.supports: Original Fig. 3 participants 797, 841 and 880; lang_LH_netw; bySessVoxZ; 1,000 baseline plus 250 drive plus 250 suppress sentences.

evidence.locator: Argument defaults and LOAD NEURAL TARGET block
evidence.supports: Original training IDs, last-token GPT2-XL layer 22, ridgeCV, Pearson metric, participant averaging and declared fMRI processing parameters.
Author item-level averaging and Pearson plotting calculation route; run not executed.
The canonical source task includes held-out-participant drive/suppress response effects and linguistic-feature controls; Fig.3 correlation alone does not cover that registered scope.

target.description: Refit sentence-feature-to-fMRI encoding, preserve the original held-out-participant drive/suppress response-effect analysis and linguistic-feature controls, and compare the existing Fig. 3 sentence-prediction endpoint. The proposed correlation endpoint does not silently replace the rest of the canonical scope. Fig. 3 prediction and Fig. 2 response effects are source-identified; the exact final-publication binding of all linguistic-control outputs remains unresolved.

dataset.description: Author OSF ru38b release as loaded by brain-lang-data_participant_20230728.csv and associated GPT2-XL last-token activations; raw fMRI, blocked data and supplementary modify data are distinct assets.

cohort.description: Train IDs 848, 853, 865, 875 and 876; original main evaluation IDs 797, 841 and 880. The two other released event-related evaluation participants and four blocked-design participants are not interchangeable with this cohort.

split.description: Train the encoding map on the original five-person 1,000-sentence baseline response set; evaluate on the original three-person 1,500-sentence search set. The 1,000 baseline sentences recur across people; only the 500 drive/suppress sentences are new stimuli. New nested splits are extensions.

inputs.description: Sentence text/representations and the original train-participant responses. Author comparator uses GPT2-XL last-token layer-22 features with ridge regression. Evaluation response columns and saved source predictions are operator-side assessment artifacts.

preprocessing.description: Match the released GLMsingle response extraction and bySessVoxZ normalization; retain the functionally localized lang_LH_netw target rather than switching to an anatomical ROI or a voxel subset. Source script records the exact extraction parameter identifiers.

metric.description: Pearson correlation r=sum((prediction-mean(prediction))*(response-mean(response)))/sqrt(sum((prediction-mean(prediction))^2)*sum((response-mean(response))^2)) across the original 1,500 sentence items.

aggregation.description: Average the three original evaluation participants per sentence within lang_LH_netw before calculating one pooled correlation; baseline-only and condition-wise correlations are separately reported diagnostics, not alternative winning endpoints.

comparison.primary_metric: Fig. 3 Pearson correlation across the original 1,500 sentence-level mean evaluation responses

published_baseline.description: Author preprint v4 reports r=0.43 for this endpoint (baseline-only r=0.30). The final Nature figure caption confirms the task but its numeric coefficient was not independently recovered; do not substitute 0.38 training-split predictivity, 0.62 simulated ceiling, or drive/suppress effect sizes.

reproduced_author_baseline.description: Author fit/apply and figure code provide a reproducible route, but no source-matched original Fig. 3 replay receipt is admitted here. Existing prescribed ridge/LOOCV reconstruction evidence is a different grading target.

minimum_effect.rationale: Resolve the final source coefficient and reproduce it before choosing a meaningful prediction gain. The noise-ceiling simulation, p-value and arbitrary increment cannot define the improvement margin.

uncertainty.method: Predeclare a paired candidate-minus-author correlation comparison with dependence-aware uncertainty over sentences and participants; report the fixed three-person estimand separately from population generalization.
uncertainty.independent_unit: Sentence stimulus crossed with participant; only three independent evaluation people
uncertainty.rationale: Pooling 4,500 rows as independent would duplicate stimuli and people. Source significance against zero does not test improvement over the author model.

paper_win_requires: Recover and bind the final-publication numeric result to the exact original Fig. 3 task before admission.
Replay the source-author encoding model under the same feature/data access and retain a distinct measured author score.
Compare a frozen candidate on all original 1,500 search stimuli and all three original participants with the identical response normalization and pooling.
Exceed both the source-paper and replayed author comparator under a justified effect and predeclared uncertainty rule.
Do not count smaller reference discrepancy, stronger condition p-values, a noise-ceiling ratio, a new split, a reduced stimulus set, or the two-person modify panel as the original paper win.
A claim of improved stimulus control requires neural responses to candidate-selected stimuli under the source protocol; offline prediction improvements alone do not establish that intervention.

Retain the source held-out-participant drive/suppress effect analyses and linguistic-feature controls as mandatory calibration/safeguard outputs, with the original experiment identities and response definitions. Stronger p-values or larger coefficients do not count as improvement.

Resolve and register the full canonical-scope success rule before admission; a higher Fig. 3 correlation alone is insufficient for a whole-registration paper win. The old claim-evidence report roster is preserved, not replaced by one correlation.

current_sota.description: No current-SOTA claim is made; a different language-encoding dataset or cross-validation protocol is not a comparator for this source experiment.

episode.improvement_loop: Once the final source baseline is recovered, develop encoding changes on original train-participant data with training-only validation and a declared feature/model exposure policy. Treat published targets and cached predictions as known exposures that require isolation.
episode.candidate_freeze: Seal feature model, preprocessing, fitting/selection recipe and prediction code before original evaluation responses are supplied to the trusted evaluator.
episode.final_evaluation: One fixed-protocol comparison on the full original main search set; show source-paper, replayed author and candidate scores separately. No current executable success condition is claimed. Include the original drive/suppress response effects and linguistic-feature controls as calibration/safeguards; no whole-registration victory follows from Fig. 3 alone.
episode.baseline_policy: Use the pinned author fit/apply/figure route and preserve its original train/evaluation identities. A locally rewritten ridge baseline, historical numeric-tolerance grader or exploratory modify comparison is not the paper baseline.

blocking_issues: Exact final-publication Fig. 3 numeric baseline needs confirmation against the primary final paper or a qualified author replay.
Author-model replay and metric/source release hashes are not bound to an improvement evaluator.
Publicly exposed evaluation responses and source predictions need a versioned enforced access policy.
Effect size, dependence-aware uncertainty rule and fixed resource/query budgets remain unresolved.
Historical registered-runtime score verifies prescribed reconstruction, not arbitrary candidate prediction improvement.
The full canonical scope includes response-control effects and linguistic-feature controls; their calibration/safeguard obligations and relation to an overall success decision are not yet bound.

legacy.notes: Preserve registered-runtime and claim-evidence materials, all historical ridge/LOOCV and mixed-model checks, and their exposure history. They remain reconstruction/calibration components; prospective or retrospectively isolated improvement requires separate admission.
